access_requirements: The user must approve Android VpnService and explicitly enable the VPN; the service must run with the required foreground notification/lifecycle.
A packet parser and routing implementation must be built; VpnService exposes a TUN packet interface, not ready-made flow events.
evidence_source: Parsed IP packets and flow metadata read from SVS-Cyber’s user-authorized VpnService TUN interface; protocol-specific visibility varies.
distribution_restrictions: Google Play requires the VpnService declaration and listing documentation; sensitive data collection requires a separate prominent in-app disclosure and affirmative consent.
limitations: Only traffic routed through the active VPN is observable; another VPN, excluded apps or a stopped/revoked service create blind spots.
No HTTPS decryption. DoH/DoT, QUIC, encrypted ClientHello and hard-coded IPs can hide DNS names or reduce metadata.
Per-app attribution is not guaranteed; report unknown when Android or the packet path does not identify an owner.
Monitoring requires an active foreground service and can be stopped by the user, Android or OEM power management.

access_requirements: Android Enterprise device owner on a fully managed device, or profile owner of an organization-owned managed profile where supported; retrieve only events exposed by Android SecurityLog.
Security logging must be enabled by the authorized DPC and batches are delivered/retrieved by Android; this is batched audit logging, not a continuous EDR feed.
evidence_source: DevicePolicyManager.setSecurityLoggingEnabled/retrieveSecurityLogs and documented SecurityLog event tags, within the enrolled management scope.
limitations: Not available on unmanaged consumer installs. Device-wide process/security events are limited to fully managed single-user/affiliated-device scope; organization-owned managed profiles expose only supported managed-profile events, with some events redacted or omitted.
Do not report events that the Android version/device does not emit or the enrolled profile is not allowed to expose.

name: Managed Package Events
description: Reads documented package-management audit records from authorized Android SecurityLog batches where available; coverage is OS/event-tag dependent.
access_requirements: Android Enterprise device owner on a fully managed device, or profile owner of an organization-owned managed profile where supported; retrieve only events exposed by Android SecurityLog.
Security logging must be enabled by the authorized DPC and batches are delivered/retrieved by Android; this is batched audit logging, not a continuous EDR feed.
evidence_source: DevicePolicyManager.setSecurityLoggingEnabled/retrieveSecurityLogs and documented SecurityLog event tags, within the enrolled management scope.
limitations: Not available on unmanaged consumer installs. Device-wide process/security events are limited to fully managed single-user/affiliated-device scope; organization-owned managed profiles expose only supported managed-profile events, with some events redacted or omitted.
Do not report events that the Android version/device does not emit or the enrolled profile is not allowed to expose.

name: Managed Security Policy
description: Reports the security policy states that an authorized DPC can inspect; no general system policy-change event stream is exposed.
access_requirements: Device/profile owner or properly delegated Android Enterprise DPC with authority to read the specific policy state.
Policy reads are limited to settings the enrolled DPC can inspect; not available to an unmanaged consumer app.
evidence_source: DevicePolicyManager policy-state APIs for the policies explicitly enforced or observable by the authorized DPC.
limitations: Only DPC-manageable policy state is in scope; no general system policy-change log is exposed.
Requires managed enrollment and applicable owner/delegation role; no consumer-app access.

name: Enterprise Logging Health
description: Detects logging failures, unavailable log batches or disabled enterprise logging.
access_requirements: Authorized device owner or supported organization-owned profile owner must have security/network logging enabled and permit batch retrieval.
Health is inferred from DPC enablement, callbacks, retrieval results and batch timestamps; logging is not a continuous stream.
evidence_source: DevicePolicyManager logging enabled state, onSecurityLogsAvailable/onNetworkLogsAvailable callbacks, batch retrieval outcomes and last successful retrieval time.
limitations: Health describes the authorized logging pipeline only; Android may batch, delay or discard logs.
A missing batch is not proof that no events occurred.
